data.title: Musk threatens Democrats teeing up congressional probes
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Elon Musk, President Donald Trump's multi-billionaire ally, on Wednesday threatened Democrats who want to investigate alleged corruption and his role in the US government if they win control of Congress next month.

data.title: Quebec separatist premier sworn in without royal presence
data.description: MONTREAL (CANADA) - Quebec's new separatist leader took office Wednesday after being sworn in without pledging an oath to King Charles III, while the monarch's official representative in the Canadian province stayed away from the ceremony.

data.title: Washington orders US embassy staff, families to leave Saudi Arabia
data.description: RIYADH (SAUDI ARABIA) - Washington has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis.

data.title: Judge orders Meta to pay $25 bn to New Mexico in Cambridge Analytica case
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - A New Mexico judge ruled Wednesday that Meta must pay $25 billion to the state after a jury found last month that the social media giant had deceived users in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, according to media reports.

data.title: Maradona doctor was made 'scapegoat' for his death, Argentine court told
data.description: SAN ISIDRO (ARGENTINA) - A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a "scapegoat."

data.title: UN says El Nino indicators already ‘off the charts’
data.description: GENEVA - The El Nino weather phenomenon gripping the planet is heading off the charts, the United Nations warned on Wednesday, saying countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.

data.title: Rightists worldwide blame immigrants for French crisis
data.description: PARIS - Right-wing politicians around the world have seized on France’s riots, casting immigration as the culprit ahead of tense elections testing their own populist credentials.

data.title: Visiting Argentine president calls Spanish PM a ‘dictator’
data.description: MADRID - Argentina’s far-right President Javier Milei called Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez a “dictator” in a visit to Madrid on Wednesday, urging voters to oust the Socialist leader in upcoming elections.

data.title: Japan sends diplomat to Russia over detained journalist
data.description: TOKYO — Japan has sent a senior diplomat to Moscow to discuss the release of a journalist detained by Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said on Wednesday.

data.title: Five things to know about Chinese AI firm DeepSeek
data.description: BEIJING - The United States Department of Homeland Security this week ordered government agencies to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China.

data.title: Five things to know about Chinese AI firm DeepSeek
data.description: BEIJING - The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China.

data.title: Macron decries ‘stupid’ comments on France riots
data.description: DOHA - President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday criticised world leaders for making “stupid” comments about the rioting on the sidelines of protests in France, in an apparent swipe at US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

data.title: Celebrity shark steered out of South Korean canal
data.description: SEOUL - A shark that has become a viral sensation in South Korea was coaxed out of a canal in which it was stuck, authorities said on Wednesday, as falling temperatures raised concerns for its survival.

data.title: President berates countries that ‘insult’ Indonesia over toxic haze
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesia’s president lashed out on Wednesday against “countries that like to insult” his nation over wildfires that have razed vast areas, spewing toxic haze into neighbouring countries.

data.title: Japan sends senior diplomat to Russia over detained journalist
data.description: TOKYO — Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist detained by Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said on Wednesday.

data.title: Record-late 30°C heat grips wide swathe of Japan
data.description: KYODO — A wide swath of Japan faced sweltering heat on Wednesday, with temperatures in some regions recording the latest day in the year to top 30 degrees Celsius, prompting many to switch back to summer clothes for the day.

data.title: North Korea says 'new firepower units' in place after border threat
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea has moved new units into "firing positions", the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un said Wednesday, days after Pyongyang warned it was considering deploying additional strike means to its border with South Korea.

data.title: UK approves new North Sea gas drilling
data.description: LONDON - The UK government said on Wednesday that it had approved plans to begin drilling in a controversial new gas field in the North Sea, ending months of speculation about the future of the site.

data.title: 'Daily struggle': Cubans dig wells in search of water
data.description: HAVANA — Kevin Martinez has come up with a creative new way to avoid shutting his restaurant when water runs low in Cuba, a common source of frustration for the business owner.

data.title: Malaysia bans civil servants from using Israeli mapping app
data.description: KUALA ​LUMPUR — Malaysia has banned civil servants ​from using Alphabet's navigation application Waze after Prime ​Minister Anwar Ibrahim ‌said its origins in Israel raised security concerns.

data.title: World falling 'dangerously short' on climate action: UN chief
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century, the UN warned on Wednesday.

data.title: South Korea launches new bid to guide crowd-pulling shark to sea
data.description: SEOUL - South Korean authorities began a new attempt Wednesday to coax a shark-turned-viral sensation back to sea, with falling temperatures in the Busan canal where it is stranded raising concerns for its survival.

data.title: US envoy to meet Russia's president after 'productive' talks with Zelensky
data.description: SAINT PETERSBURG — US envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Saint Petersburgand meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday following "very productive" talks with Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.

data.title: French PM to meet unions as government prepares for more protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - France's prime minister plans to meet unions on Wednesday to discuss security and has vowed a "massive" police deployment at protests, following riots in the past week that led to curfews and arrests.

data.title: 'To the shelter, quickly!' Air raids reshape Kyiv school life
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - When the air raid alert sounded over the Kyiv region, children knew exactly what to do: they grabbed their tiny backpacks and ran towards the shelter, abandoning bikes, toys and even a doll on the school playground.

data.title: Musk backs SpaceX-Tesla merger as rocket firm turns profit
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Elon Musk said Tuesday he would back a merger of SpaceX and Tesla, as his rocket and AI company reported its first quarterly profit since going public, driven by deals to rent out computing power to AI firms.

data.title: Meta says it complied with Brazil court order to treat candidates equally
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - US tech giant Meta said Tuesday it had complied with a Brazilian court order to treat the election campaigns of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro equally.

data.title: Alberta separatists vow to fight on, risking turmoil for Canada
data.description: EDMONTON (CANADA) - Separatists in Canada's Alberta province say their independence fight is not over despite a decisive referendum loss, risking long-term political turmoil in an oil-rich province crucial to the Canadian economy.
